name: Reuel (Son of Esau and Bashemath)
title: Son of Esau and Edomite tribal founder
summary: Reuel was the second son of Esau and his wife Bashemath (daughter of Ishmael). He became the father of four sons who served as tribal chiefs in Edom. Through his lineage, he connected the family lines of Esau and Ishmael and played an important role in early Edomite history.

keyEvents.title: The Birth of Reuel
keyEvents.description: Reuel was born as the son of Esau and Bashemath, Ishmael's daughter, in the land of Canaan.

keyEvents.title: Reuel's Sons Are Mentioned
keyEvents.description: Reuel's four sons—Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah—are listed as his descendants.

keyEvents.title: Esau's Family Moves to Seir
keyEvents.description: Esau took his wives, sons, and daughters, including Reuel, and settled in the hill country of Seir, away from his brother Jacob.

keyEvents.title: Reuel's Sons Become Clan Chiefs
keyEvents.description: Reuel's sons became clan chiefs in Edom: Chief Nahath, Chief Zerah, Chief Shammah, and Chief Mizzah. These are counted as Reuel's chiefs in the land of Edom.

keyEvents.title: Esau's Genealogy as the Father of Edom
keyEvents.description: Reuel is mentioned as part of Esau's genealogy, showing that Esau was the ancestor of Edom and that his descendants became a great people in the hill country of Seir.

keyEvents.title: The Ancestors of Edom in Chronicles
keyEvents.description: Reuel's lineage is repeated in Chronicles as part of the complete overview of Esau's descendants and the tribal chiefs of Edom.
